parsed.why: No trans-specific criminalisation or documented targeting, but foreign-document mismatches recur at inspections and there is no guidance or remedy. General stigma and thin evidence temper the otherwise limited visitor-facing risk.

Same-sex conduct is criminalised under an authoritarian government, with official hostility, closed advocacy space and no trans protections. The law is not trans-specific and no visitor enforcement is documented, but these structural signals imply substantial exposure.

Trans women in at least one jail face birth-sex placement, head-shaving and abuse risks; police have also arrested peaceful Pride participants, and recent killings add concern. Local protections and a safer jail annex do not resolve national exposure.

No trans-specific enforcement or violence is documented; social evidence is sparse and mostly resident-facing. The clearest visitor concern is possible document mismatch at a border, without evidence of routine targeting or adverse handling.

Documented airport questioning and detention can out trans travelers; prison isolation and recent reports of anti-LGBTQ violence add risk. Protections and court relief operate, but do not erase these concrete exposures.
